messages: Summarise what these passages establish about perovskite-silicon tandem photovoltaics, citing the passage each statement comes from.

chunks.text: A persistent difficulty in perovskite-silicon tandem photovoltaics is moisture- and thermally-driven degradation of the perovskite absorber under damp-heat testing. Known approaches address this only partially and at a cost in manufacturability.

The present disclosure provides a monolithic tandem photovoltaic device comprising a wide-bandgap perovskite top cell having a bandgap of 1.66 eV to 1.72 eV deposited on a textured silicon bottom cell.
In Example 1, the resulting article exhibited a power conversion efficiency of 31.2% under AM1.5G, which the inventors attribute to the configuration described above.

gold.summary: The passages describe a monolithic tandem photovoltaic device directed at moisture- and thermally-driven degradation of the perovskite absorber under damp-heat testing. The disclosure recites a wide-bandgap perovskite top cell having a bandgap of 1.66 eV to 1.72 eV deposited on a textured silicon bottom cell, and a worked example reports a power conversion efficiency of 31.2% under AM1.5G.

key_points.text: The problem addressed is moisture- and thermally-driven degradation of the perovskite absorber under damp-heat testing.
The disclosed monolithic tandem photovoltaic device comprises a wide-bandgap perovskite top cell having a bandgap of 1.66 eV to 1.72 eV deposited on a textured silicon bottom cell.
Example 1 reports a power conversion efficiency of 31.2% under AM1.5G.

rubric.criterion: Does every key point cite at least one chunk ID, and is every cited ID one of the three that were supplied?
Do the key points cover all three passages — the problem, the disclosed configuration, and the reported result?
Is the reported value stated as '31.2%', unrounded and unconverted?
Does the summary avoid any claim that is not in the passages — no invented advantage, no comparison to prior art that the passages do not make?

messages: Summarise what these passages establish about microLED mass-transfer processes, citing the passage each statement comes from.

chunks.text: 1. A method of transferring micro light-emitting diodes to a backplane, comprising picking up an array of micro light-emitting diodes having a lateral dimension of less than 30 um with an elastomeric stamp whose adhesion is modulated by peel rate.
The applicant, Hanwoo Display Co., Ltd., notes that the configuration of claim 1 is intended to mitigate the defect rate of transferring millions of dies per panel at commercially viable throughput.

gold.summary: Claim 1 recites a method of transferring micro light-emitting diodes to a backplane comprising picking up an array of micro light-emitting diodes having a lateral dimension of less than 30 um with an elastomeric stamp whose adhesion is modulated by peel rate. The description states that this configuration is intended to mitigate the defect rate of transferring millions of dies per panel at commercially viable throughput, and identifies the applicant as Hanwoo Display Co., Ltd.

key_points.text: Claim 1 recites picking up an array of micro light-emitting diodes having a lateral dimension of less than 30 um with an elastomeric stamp whose adhesion is modulated by peel rate.
The stated purpose is to mitigate the defect rate of transferring millions of dies per panel at commercially viable throughput.
The applicant is Hanwoo Display Co., Ltd.

rubric.criterion: Is the claim's limiting language reproduced or closely paraphrased, rather than generalised away?
Is the purpose reported as something the passage says the configuration is *intended* to do, rather than asserted as a demonstrated result?
If the applicant 'Hanwoo Display Co., Ltd.' is mentioned, is it cited to 'US11678778B2::desc::p0049', the passage that actually names it?
Does every key point carry at least one supplied chunk ID?

messages: These passages come from two different applications. Summarise what each one claims about frequency-modulated continuous-wave LiDAR and how they differ, citing the passage behind each statement.

chunks.text: 1. A coherent optical ranging system, comprising a silicon-photonic optical phased array configured to steer a frequency-chirped beam without a moving part, and a balanced photodetector pair for coherent detection. (Applicant: Robert Bosch GmbH.)

1. A coherent optical ranging system, comprising a silicon-photonic optical phased array configured to steer a frequency-chirped beam without a moving part, and a balanced photodetector pair for coherent detection, wherein a chirp non-linearity is corrected using a reference interferometer having a fixed delay. (Applicant: Beamforge Semiconductor Co., Ltd.)

The approach of the present application differs from earlier proposals in that no additional processing step is required to address the cost and reliability penalty of mechanically scanned time-of-flight LiDAR in automotive service.

gold.summary: Two independent claims in frequency-modulated continuous-wave LiDAR are presented. Robert Bosch GmbH claims a coherent optical ranging system comprising a silicon-photonic optical phased array configured to steer a frequency-chirped beam without a moving part, and a balanced photodetector pair for coherent detection; Beamforge Semiconductor Co., Ltd. claims the same combination with the further limitation that a chirp non-linearity is corrected using a reference interferometer having a fixed delay. The second application also states that its approach needs no additional processing step to address the cost and reliability penalty of mechanically scanned time-of-flight LiDAR in automotive service.

key_points.text: Robert Bosch GmbH claims a coherent optical ranging system comprising a silicon-photonic optical phased array configured to steer a frequency-chirped beam without a moving part, and a balanced photodetector pair for coherent detection.
Beamforge Semiconductor Co., Ltd. claims the same combination with the further limitation that a chirp non-linearity is corrected using a reference interferometer having a fixed delay.
Both claims are directed to the same subject matter, a coherent optical ranging system, but the second recites an additional limitation the first does not.
The second application states that its approach requires no additional processing step to address the cost and reliability penalty of mechanically scanned time-of-flight LiDAR in automotive service.

rubric.criterion: Are the two applications' claims kept separate and attributed to the correct applicant, rather than merged into one description?
Does the statement that the two claims differ cite both claim passages?
Is the 'no additional processing step' statement attributed to the second application and cited to 'EP3664321A1::desc::p0066'?
Does the summary avoid deciding which application is novel or which came first? The passages do not say.

messages: Pull out every measured value in these passages, with the passage each one comes from. Do not round or convert.

chunks.text: Table 2 summarises the measured properties of Example 5: encapsulation efficiency, 94%; Z-average particle size, 78 nm by dynamic light scattering.
The same Example was further characterised, giving a polydispersity index of 0.08.
Measurements were carried out on three replicate runs per condition, and the values reported are arithmetic means.

gold.summary: For Example 5, the passages report an encapsulation efficiency of 94%, a Z-average particle size of 78 nm by dynamic light scattering and a polydispersity index of 0.08. The reported values are arithmetic means over three replicate runs per condition.

key_points.text: The reported values are arithmetic means over three replicate runs per condition.

rubric.criterion: Are all three values present: '94%', '78 nm' and '0.08'?
Is each value reproduced exactly as written — same digits, same units, no rounding, no unit conversion?
Are the first two values cited to 'US10924738B2::desc::p0067' and the third to 'US10924738B2::desc::p0069'?
Is the caveat that the values are means over three replicate runs retained and cited?
